newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PSE steady, investors watch political scuffle.
newsitem.headline: Czech PSE steady, investors watch political scuffle.

text.p: Growing political uncertainty kept the Prague Stock Exchange in check on Thursday, as the PX50 index closed down 0.1 point at 497.6.

Most major shares saw little movement in their prices after posting moderate gains one day earlier, with investors taking a wait and see attitude ahead of an expected confidence vote for the government of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus next week.

"It looks like many investors are going to wait to see the result of the confidence vote and then based on that, they will either take or not take positions," said Lubos Vystavel, a trader at ING Barings in Prague.

One of the most serious assaults in recent days came from Deputy Premier Josef Lux, the chairman of the centrist KDU-CSL, who claimed that Klaus intentionally withheld from ministers a fax written by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) warning earlier this year of a possible currency crisis.
Klaus denied that he withheld the IMF's warning from ministers, but his deputy party chairman, Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec, corroborated Lux's claim.
Zieleniec's statement sparked a rash of local media reports that an internal power struggle was blazing within the ODS.
Klaus's party called on coalition partners on Thursday to support their agreed emergency economic programme as internal rifts threatened to split the centre-right government.
Total volume was thin at 686,251 shares on turnover of 675.5 million crowns. Overall, 124 issues gained ground, while 92 fell and 39 were unchanged.

Komercni Banka's uptrend of recent days came to a halt despite a promising beginning to the day, with the bank's shares gaining 20 crowns at the bourse fixing before retreating to close down two at 1,988.
SPT Telecom, bank IPB, and CEZ also closed lower.
Shares of cigarette maker Tabak and confectioner Cokolodavny posted strong gains of 276 crowns and 105 crowns respectively.
